units.name: public-api
units.role: One-call convenience functions (get, post, ...) that wrap Session for a single request.
units.description: This is the simple front door of the library: the get, post, put, patch, delete, head, options, and request functions that most people type when they want to fetch or send something over the web. Each one quietly creates a short-lived session, uses it to send exactly one request, and hands back the response, closing the connection afterward. It must never keep connections open between calls, or implement its own retry, authentication, or parsing logic - all of that belongs to the session and request/response machinery it calls into.

entrypoints.name: request
entrypoints.plain: Send one HTTP request of the given method and return the Response.

entrypoints.name: get
entrypoints.plain: Send a GET request.

entrypoints.name: options
entrypoints.plain: Send an OPTIONS request.

entrypoints.name: head
entrypoints.plain: Send a HEAD request; does not follow redirects unless told to.

entrypoints.name: put

entrypoints.name: patch

entrypoints.name: delete
entrypoints.plain: Send a DELETE request.

units.name: package-bootstrap
units.role: Runs at import time to verify dependency compatibility, patch in SNI support when needed, and assemble the public requests namespace.
units.description: This is the code that runs the instant someone writes 'import requests'. Before anything else happens, it checks that the versions of a few supporting libraries this package relies on (urllib3, and either chardet or charset_normalizer for guessing text encodings) are ones it knows how to work with, and prints a friendly warning if they look mismatched. On older systems whose built-in secure-connection support is missing a needed feature, it quietly swaps in a replacement so secure websites still work. It also silences some noisy warnings from other libraries, and finally gathers the pieces built in the rest of the package - the get/post functions, the Session class, error types, status codes - into the single 'requests' module everyone imports. It must never implement request or response logic itself; its only job is bootstrapping and version-checking.

entrypoints.name: check_compatibility
entrypoints.plain: Runs automatically at import time to confirm installed urllib3/chardet/charset_normalizer versions are supported; not meant to be called directly by users.

effects.description: Emits process-wide warnings.warn(RequestsDependencyWarning) when installed urllib3/chardet/charset_normalizer/cryptography versions look unsupported, and mutates the global warnings-filter table to silence urllib3's DependencyWarning and re-enable FileModeWarning by default.
Monkeypatches urllib3 at import time via pyopenssl.inject_into_urllib3() when the platform's ssl module lacks SNI support, changing how all subsequent TLS connections negotiate.
Attaches a logging.NullHandler to the 'requests' logger so the process doesn't print Python's default 'No handler found' message.

units.name: request-response-model
units.role: Turn caller-supplied URL/headers/params/body into a ready-to-send request, and turn raw transport output into an inspectable Response.
units.description: This unit is the heart of what it means to make a web request in this library. It defines the Request a caller wants to send, the fully-formed PreparedRequest that is actually put on the wire (URL cleaned up, headers set, cookies attached, body encoded as JSON, form data, or a multipart file upload), and the Response object representing what came back from the server (status code, headers, cookies, and a body that can be read as raw bytes, text, JSON, or streamed a chunk or line at a time). It does not open sockets or talk to the network itself - it hands the prepared request to a transport component to be sent, and turns whatever that transport gives back into the friendly Response object application code interacts with.

entrypoints.name: Request
entrypoints.plain: Describes a request the caller wants to make: method, url, headers, data, and so on.

entrypoints.name: Request.prepare
entrypoints.plain: Turn a Request into a PreparedRequest ready to send.

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest
entrypoints.plain: The fully-formed request that actually gets sent to the server.

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest.prepare

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest.copy

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest.prepare_url

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest.prepare_headers
entrypoints.plain: Normalize and validate the request headers.

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest.prepare_body
entrypoints.plain: Encode form data, JSON, or file uploads into the request body.

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest.prepare_content_length

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest.prepare_auth
entrypoints.plain: Attach authentication to the request.

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest.prepare_cookies

entrypoints.name: PreparedRequest.prepare_hooks
entrypoints.plain: Register the caller's event hooks on the request.

entrypoints.name: Response
entrypoints.plain: Represents what the server sent back: status, headers, cookies, and body.

entrypoints.plain: The next PreparedRequest in a redirect chain, if any.

entrypoints.name: Response.iter_content
entrypoints.plain: Stream the response body in chunks without loading it all into memory.

entrypoints.name: Response.iter_lines
entrypoints.plain: Stream the response body one line at a time.

entrypoints.name: Response.content
entrypoints.plain: The full response body as bytes.

entrypoints.name: Response.text
entrypoints.plain: The response body decoded to a string using the detected or declared encoding.

entrypoints.name: Response.json
entrypoints.plain: Parse the response body as JSON.

entrypoints.name: Response.raise_for_status
entrypoints.plain: Raise an HTTPError if the response was an error status.

entrypoints.name: Response.close
entrypoints.plain: Release the underlying network connection back to the pool.

effects.description: Reads user-supplied file-like objects (fp.read()) to build multipart upload bodies, and probes them via super_len()/tell() to determine content length.
Response.iter_content reads bytes directly off the underlying urllib3 HTTPResponse/socket stream (self.raw.stream()/.read()) to materialize the response body.

units.name: session
units.role: Own the Session object that merges defaults with per-call options, picks an adapter, sends the request, and follows redirects.
units.description: This is the part of the library that acts like a persistent conversation with servers. When you create a Session, it remembers things like cookies, custom headers, login credentials, and proxy settings so you don't have to repeat them on every call. When you ask it to fetch a URL, it combines your one-off instructions with those remembered defaults, figures out which piece of connection-handling machinery (adapter) should talk to that URL, hands off the request, times how long it took, saves any cookies the server sent back, and automatically follows redirect responses until it reaches a final answer - stripping login credentials when a redirect points to a different site so they are not leaked.

entrypoints.name: Session
entrypoints.plain: A reusable client that remembers cookies, headers, auth, and proxies across multiple requests.

entrypoints.name: Session.prepare_request

entrypoints.name: Session.request
entrypoints.plain: Prepare and send a request of any method, following redirects.

entrypoints.name: Session.send

entrypoints.name: Session.get_adapter

entrypoints.name: Session.mount
entrypoints.plain: Register a transport adapter for a URL prefix.

entrypoints.name: SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects
entrypoints.plain: Follow a chain of redirect responses until a final response is reached.

entrypoints.name: SessionRedirectMixin.should_strip_auth

entrypoints.name: session

units.name: auth
units.role: Compute the Authorization/Proxy-Authorization header for an outgoing request: HTTP Basic, Proxy, and Digest authentication.
units.description: This part of the library knows how to prove who you are to a website or proxy server that asks for a username and password. It supports the two most common ways servers ask for credentials: Basic authentication (encode the username and password) and Digest authentication (a back-and-forth where the server issues a challenge and the client computes a scrambled answer using the password, without ever sending the password itself). When a request needs authentication, this code builds the header that gets attached to it, and for Digest it also drives the extra round trip where the server first rejects the request with a challenge and a properly-authenticated request is sent back automatically.

entrypoints.name: AuthBase
entrypoints.plain: Base class for a callable that attaches authentication to a request.

entrypoints.name: HTTPBasicAuth.__call__
entrypoints.plain: Attach a Basic-auth Authorization header to a request.

entrypoints.name: HTTPDigestAuth.handle_redirect
entrypoints.plain: Reset saved Digest state when a request is redirected.

entrypoints.name: HTTPDigestAuth.handle_401
entrypoints.plain: On a 401 challenge, compute the Digest response and resend the request.

entrypoints.name: HTTPDigestAuth.__call__
entrypoints.plain: Attach Digest auth to a request, registering the 401-handling hook.

entrypoints.name: _basic_auth_str
entrypoints.plain: Build the value of a Basic-auth header from a username and password. Named as private but imported directly by the session and adapters units - see violations_observed.

effects.description: os.urandom(8) supplies randomness mixed into the Digest auth client-nonce (cnonce) computation.
time.ctime() is folded into the cnonce entropy source.
threading.local() keeps per-thread Digest auth state (nonce count, last nonce, retry counter) so one HTTPDigestAuth instance is safe to share across threads.

units.name: exceptions
units.role: Define the vocabulary of errors and warnings requests can raise.
units.description: This file is the library's catalog of everything that can go wrong when making a web request, and gives each kind of problem its own named label - an invalid or missing web address, a connection that couldn't be established, a request that took too long, being redirected too many times, a response body that claims to be JSON but isn't, and a few others. These labels are organized in a family tree so a program using this library can catch a very specific problem or a broad category with one line of code. It also defines a couple of warning types used to flag less severe, non-fatal issues.

entrypoints.name: RequestException
entrypoints.plain: Base class for all errors raised while handling a request.

entrypoints.name: InvalidJSONError

entrypoints.name: JSONDecodeError

entrypoints.name: HTTPError

entrypoints.name: ConnectionError

entrypoints.name: ProxyError

entrypoints.name: SSLError

entrypoints.name: Timeout

entrypoints.name: ConnectTimeout

entrypoints.name: ReadTimeout

entrypoints.name: URLRequired
entrypoints.plain: Raised when a valid web address is required but none was given.

entrypoints.name: TooManyRedirects
entrypoints.plain: Raised when a request is redirected more times than allowed.

entrypoints.name: MissingSchema

entrypoints.name: InvalidSchema

entrypoints.name: InvalidURL

entrypoints.name: InvalidHeader

entrypoints.name: InvalidProxyURL

entrypoints.name: ChunkedEncodingError

entrypoints.name: ContentDecodingError

entrypoints.name: StreamConsumedError

entrypoints.name: RetryError
entrypoints.plain: Raised when custom retry logic fails.

entrypoints.name: UnrewindableBodyError

entrypoints.name: RequestsWarning
entrypoints.plain: Base warning category for non-fatal issues.

entrypoints.name: FileModeWarning

entrypoints.name: RequestsDependencyWarning
entrypoints.plain: Warns when an installed dependency version is outside the expected range.

units.name: status-codes
units.role: A friendly lookup table mapping HTTP status codes to their names.
units.description: This file is a dictionary of HTTP status codes, like a phonebook that lets other parts of the program refer to web response codes by easy-to-remember names (such as 'not_found' or 'ok') instead of memorizing the number, like 404 or 200. It builds a single shared lookup object called 'codes' that other parts of the library and end users can consult to check or compare status codes in a readable way.

entrypoints.name: codes
entrypoints.plain: The shared lookup object mapping HTTP status code numbers to friendly names, e.g. codes.not_found == 404.

units.name: cookies
units.role: Bridge requests' dict-like cookie model to Python's standard-library http.cookiejar machinery.
units.description: This file is the translator between the friendly, dictionary-style way requests lets you look at cookies (small pieces of data websites ask a client to remember) and the more rigid cookie-jar system built into Python. It knows how to read the 'Set-Cookie' instructions a server sends back, store them in memory, merge cookies from different sources (like a session's saved cookies and a one-off request's cookies), and figure out which cookies should be attached to a future request to the same site. It does not save cookies to disk itself or talk to the network directly; it only manages cookies already sitting in memory as part of a request or response.

entrypoints.name: CookieConflictError
entrypoints.plain: Raised when a cookie name is ambiguous across multiple domains/paths in the jar.

entrypoints.name: RequestsCookieJar
entrypoints.plain: A cookie jar you can also use like a dictionary.

entrypoints.name: extract_cookies_to_jar
entrypoints.plain: Read Set-Cookie headers from a response and store them in a jar.

entrypoints.name: get_cookie_header
entrypoints.plain: Build the Cookie header value to attach to an outgoing request.

entrypoints.name: _copy_cookie_jar
entrypoints.plain: Duplicate a cookie jar so it can be modified independently.

entrypoints.name: cookiejar_from_dict
entrypoints.plain: Build a RequestsCookieJar from a plain dict of name/value pairs.

entrypoints.name: merge_cookies
entrypoints.plain: Combine cookies from two sources (e.g. session and per-request) into one jar.

effects.description: Reads the system clock (time.time()) and normalizes cookie expiry timestamps (time.strptime/calendar.timegm) when converting a Set-Cookie header into a Cookie object.
Uses threading.RLock (inherited from http.cookiejar.CookieJar) to guard concurrent access to the in-memory cookie store.

units.name: adapters
units.role: Transport layer that turns a prepared HTTP request into an actual network connection and back into a Response.
units.description: This is the part of the library that does the actual talking to the internet. When you ask the library to fetch a page or send data to a server, this component opens or reuses a network connection to that server, handles proxies, checks the server's security certificate so the connection is trustworthy, sends the request over the wire, and wraps whatever comes back into a Response object the rest of the program can work with. It relies on a lower-level networking toolkit (urllib3) for the raw socket work, and mainly adds the policy layer on top: which certificates to trust, which proxy to use, how many retries to allow, and how to translate low-level network errors into this library's own error types.

entrypoints.name: BaseAdapter
entrypoints.plain: The contract a transport adapter must implement (send/close); Session programs against this to allow custom transports.

entrypoints.name: HTTPAdapter
entrypoints.plain: The default transport adapter, built on urllib3, mounted by Session for http:// and https://.

entrypoints.name: HTTPAdapter.send
entrypoints.plain: Send a prepared request over the network and return a Response.

entrypoints.name: HTTPAdapter.close
entrypoints.plain: Release pooled connections held by this adapter.

effects.description: Opens and pools real TCP/TLS connections to arbitrary hosts and sends requests via urllib3's PoolManager/ProxyManager; the actual wire I/O of the library, with socket handling delegated to urllib3.
cert_verify() checks that CA-bundle and client cert/key file paths exist on disk (os.path.exists/os.path.isdir) before handing them to urllib3.
Converts caller-supplied timeouts into urllib3 timeout objects that enforce connect/read wall-clock limits.

units.name: http-utils
units.role: Toolbox of stateless helper functions for URLs, headers, proxies, netrc, and upload metadata that the rest of the library leans on.
units.description: This is the library's toolbox of small, reusable helpers. It knows how to figure out how big a file someone is uploading, guess its name, clean up and reassemble web addresses, read header values like 'Link' or 'Content-Type', decide whether a request should go through a proxy by checking environment variables, and look up saved login credentials in a user's .netrc file. It does not itself send anything over the network or represent the concepts of a request or response - it is the set of small tools the parts of the library that do those things borrow from.

units.name: runtime-support
units.role: Low-level plumbing with no HTTP-specific knowledge: stdlib/optional-dependency selection, generic dict types, version metadata, the CA bundle path, and a legacy package alias.
units.description: This is a bundle of small, low-level pieces that keep the library running smoothly but have nothing to do with HTTP itself. It stores the library's own version number and author info, works out which optional helper library (chardet, charset_normalizer, or simplejson) is installed so the right one gets used, knows where to find the trusted list of security certificates, provides two general-purpose dictionary variants (one that ignores capitalization of keys, one that returns a friendly placeholder instead of crashing on a missing key), keeps very old code that imports 'requests.packages.urllib3' working, and offers small string-coercion and header-validation helpers used throughout the codebase. None of these pieces is exciting on its own, but nearly every other part of the library imports at least one of them.

It can be run directly as a command to print this report.

violations_observed.note: sessions.py imports and calls _basic_auth_str, a leading-underscore (nominally private) function in auth.py, directly to build Proxy-Authorization headers, rather than through a public auth entrypoint like HTTPBasicAuth. Recorded as a leaky abstraction, not fixed.
adapters.py likewise imports and calls the private-named auth._basic_auth_str directly to build proxy auth headers, for the same reason as the session->auth case above.

HTTPDigestAuth.handle_401 calls r.connection.send(prep, **kwargs) directly on the HTTPAdapter attached to a Response, coupling domain auth logic straight to the transport adapter's send() method instead of routing the retried request back through Session.send.

The infra-level _types.py module imports domain classes (PreparedRequest, Response, AuthBase, RequestsCookieJar) under TYPE_CHECKING to build the type aliases used across the whole library. This points the dependency arrow from infra up into domain, the reverse of the usual direction; it has no runtime effect (the block never executes), but it means the shared type vocabulary lives in a module that must know the shape of every domain unit.
